title: Beige & Maroon Block Print Kurta Set: How to Style Earthy Tones
excerpt: How to style a beige and maroon hand block print kurta set for office, festive days and winter abroad – jewellery, shoes, layering and care for cotton and Kota Doria.
body:
Beige and maroon is one of the easiest colour pairs to wear. The beige keeps it soft and calm, the maroon adds warmth and depth, and together they suit almost every skin tone, season and occasion. In a hand block print, these earthy tones look especially rich because the colour sits slightly unevenly, just like the real thing.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz Styling Team, Jaipur.*

**Quick answer**

- Beige and maroon suits every skin tone and works all year
- Gold, antique gold and oxidised silver jewellery all look good with it
- Brown, tan or maroon juttis are the easiest shoes
- In winter, layer with camel, cream, chocolate or olive
- Hand wash block printed cotton separately in cold water

## Why do earthy tones work so well?

Warm neutrals like beige, sand and khaki never look loud, so they are perfect for the office and for long days. A deep red-brown like maroon adds a festive feel without being bright. It is a colour pair that looks expensive and calm at the same time.

Our [Mitti beige and maroon block print kurta set](/products/beige-maroon-floral-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-kota-doria-dupatta-set/) is a good example: a beige cotton kurta hand block printed with maroon flowers and brown leaves, a sweetheart neckline, 3/4 sleeves, matching block print pants with a floral border, and a hand block printed Kota Doria dupatta with tassels.

## How do I style it for different days?

### Office

Skip the dupatta or fold it neatly over one shoulder. Add small gold hoops, a slim watch and a structured tan tote. Brown leather juttis or loafers keep it polished.

### Festive lunch or puja

Wear the dupatta on both arms so the printed border shows. Add oxidised silver or antique gold jhumkas, a small bindi and a stack of bangles. Maroon or gold juttis pick up the colours of the print.

### Weekend or travel

Pair the kurta with white or blue jeans and sneakers or kolhapuris for an easy, relaxed look.

### Winter abroad

Earthy tones love winter layers. Try a long camel coat, a cream cardigan or a chocolate-brown shawl, with ankle boots. See more ideas in our guide to [layering Indian outfits in winter](/blog/how-to-layer-indian-outfits-in-winter-abroad/).

## Which jewellery and colours go best?

| Goes with | Works well | Try sparingly |
|---|---|---|
| Jewellery | Gold, antique gold, oxidised silver | Bright silver |
| Shoes | Brown, tan, maroon, nude | Neon or bright white |
| Layers | Camel, cream, chocolate, olive | Black (can look heavy) |
| Lip and makeup | Nude, brick, berry | Very cool pinks |

## What is Kota Doria?

Kota Doria is a light, airy weave from Kota in Rajasthan, known for its tiny square checks. It is perfect for dupattas because it is light and drapes softly. Read more in [what Kota Doria fabric is](/blog/what-is-kota-doria-fabric-styling-and-care/).

## How do I care for a block print set?

- Hand wash separately in cold water with a mild detergent – natural block print colours may bleed a little in the first wash.
- Dry inside out in the shade.
- Iron on medium heat on the reverse side.
- Wash the Kota Doria dupatta gently and do not wring it.

Want to know how to spot real hand block print? Read [hand block print vs screen print](/blog/hand-block-print-vs-screen-print-how-to-tell-the-difference/).

## Frequently asked questions

**Does beige and maroon suit dusky skin?**
Yes – warm earthy tones flatter every skin tone, especially with gold jewellery.

**Can I wear a beige block print set to a wedding?**
It is lovely for day functions, pujas and small family events. For an evening wedding, add statement jewellery.

**Will the print fade?**
All natural prints soften a little over time. Cold water and shade drying keep the colours rich for longer.
